sentences.text: Marie Antoinette -LRB- -LSB- ˈmæriˌæntwəˈnɛt -RSB- , -LSB- ˌɑ̃ːntwə - -RSB- , -LSB- ˌɑ̃ːtwə - -RSB- , -LSB- məˈriː - -RSB- -LSB- maʁi ɑ̃twanɛt -RSB- ; born Maria Antonia Josepha Johanna -LRB- 2 November 1755 -- 16 October 1793 -RRB- was the last Queen of France and Navarre before the French Revolution .	France	French First Republic	Queen of France	Queen of France	Navarre	Queen of Navarre	French Revolution	French Revolution	Queen of France and Navarre	List of French consorts

She was born an Archduchess of Austria , and was the fifteenth and second youngest child of Empress Maria Theresa and Francis I , Holy Roman Emperor .	Austria	Habsburg Empire	Archduchess	Archduchess	Empress Maria Theresa	Empress Maria Theresa

In April 1770 , upon her marriage to Louis-Auguste , heir apparent to the French throne , she became Dauphine of France .	France	French First Republic	Louis-Auguste	Louis XVI of France	heir apparent	heir apparent	Dauphine of France	Dauphine of France

On 10 May 1774 , when her husband ascended the throne as Louis XVI , she became Queen of France and Navarre , a title she held until September 1791 , when , as the French Revolution proceeded , she became Queen of the French , a title she held until 21 September 1792 .	France	French First Republic	Queen of France	Queen of France	Navarre	Queen of Navarre	French Revolution	French Revolution	Louis XVI	Louis XVI of France	Queen of France and Navarre	List of French consorts
After eight years of marriage , Marie Antoinette gave birth to a daughter , Marie-Thérèse Charlotte , the first of her four children .	Marie-Thérèse Charlotte	Marie Thérèse of France

Despite her initial popularity , a growing number of the population eventually came to dislike her , accusing her of being profligate , promiscuous , and of harbouring sympathies for France 's enemies , particularly her native Austria .	Austria	Habsburg Empire	France	French First Republic	profligate	Spendthrift	promiscuous	promiscuous
The Diamond Necklace affair damaged her reputation further .	Diamond Necklace affair	Diamond Necklace affair

During the Revolution , she became known as Madame Déficit because the country 's financial crisis was blamed on her lavish spending and her opposition to the social and financial reforms of Turgot and Necker .	Turgot	Anne-Robert-Jacques Turgot, Baron de Laune	Necker	Jacques Necker

During the Revolution , after the government had placed the royal family under house arrest in the Tuileries Palace in October 1789 , several events linked to Marie Antoinette , in particular the June 1791 attempted flight to Varennes and her role in the War of the First Coalition , had disastrous effects on French popular opinion .	Tuileries Palace	Tuileries Palace	flight to Varennes	flight to Varennes	War of the First Coalition	War of the First Coalition

On 10 August 1792 , the attack on the Tuileries forced the royal family to take refuge at the Assembly , and on 13 August the family was imprisoned in the Temple .	10 August 1792	10 August (French Revolution)	Temple	Temple Prison
On 21 September 1792 , the monarchy was abolished .	monarchy was abolished	Proclamation of the abolition of the monarchy

After a two-day trial begun on 14 October 1793 , Marie Antoinette was convicted by the Revolutionary Tribunal of high treason and executed by guillotine on the Place de la Révolution on 16 October 1793 .
